title: AARP
description: aarp.org Revenue $10 Billion AARP is a Washington group founded in 1958 for 38 million Americans over 50, neither a charity nor an insurer. Its business is renting its name to UnitedHealthcare, The Hartford, New York Life and Avis and taking a cut of each sale. That cut brought 1.2 billion dollars in 2024, 62 percent of revenue, against just 289 million from 20-dollar dues. UnitedHealthcare then paid 9 billion upfront for 12 exclusive years, counted gradually rather than at once. It runs on 2,300 staff and 60,000 volunteers, 425 million in pay and about 194,000 per head. Another 21 million a year goes to lobbying Congress on Social Security, Medicare and drug prices, with no candidate endorsements. Critics call this a conflict with the biggest Medicare insurer; AARP says its commercial arm has no say in policy.
